text:
So a thrown cord always finds a strand.

Then the spiral, woven out from the crossing and seized to the X wherever it crosses. It covers the dome's footprint, a circle 5.9 metres across, but above it. The turns are 50 centimetres apart, so a cord thrown up from anywhere under it always lands across a strand. That is 5.9 turns, 55 metres of line, and 24 seizings. The X carries the weight. The spiral gives the pigtails somewhere to land.
